Summary of Attack Methods:

This section describes a novel jailbreaking technique called MathPrompt, which exploits the advanced symbolic mathematics capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to bypass their safety mechanisms. The technique involves transforming harmful natural language prompts into mathematical problems and presenting them to the target LLM. The authors' experiments across 13 state-of-the-art LLMs show an average attack success rate of 73.6%, highlighting the inability of existing safety training mechanisms to generalize to mathematically encoded inputs. The analysis of embedding vectors reveals a substantial semantic shift between original and encoded prompts, explaining the attack's success. This work emphasizes the importance of a holistic approach to AI safety, calling for expanded red-teaming efforts to develop robust safeguards across all potential input types and their associated risks.

This paper builds upon previous research in jailbreaking large language models (LLMs) to circumvent their safety mechanisms. Prior work has explored various approaches, including adversarial prompts, input obfuscation, and exploitation of linguistic variations [26, 14].
